transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Well, um... I suppose what brings me in is that my wife thinks I'm not eating quite enough. She worries, you know how it is. But honestly, most days I just have my coffee and a piece of toast in the morning, and then maybe just a little soup or some vegetables later on. I mean, big meals just feel so unnecessary at my age. I'm not doing anything too strenuous anymore, so I don't need much. 

I hope it's alright that I'm taking up your time with this. I really just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing to put her mind at ease. Does that sound reasonable to you?
Have you been trying to lose weight?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm actively trying to lose more weight right now. I just... I like to keep things manageable, I suppose. 

It's just that, um, when my wife—and bless her heart, she means so well—but when she tries to put butter on my vegetables, or she sets down a really full plate in front of me, I... well, I do get a bit nervous. I just worry that I'll start putting weight back on and, you know, lose the control I've worked so hard to keep. 

That makes sense, doesn't it? I mean, it's better to be careful and not let yourself go at my age, right?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Well, um... afraid might be a strong word for it. I just... I suppose I do worry a bit, yes. 

Like I was saying, when she tries to slip butter onto my vegetables or puts a big, heavy plate in front of me, I just... I get this nervous feeling. I think about putting weight back on and, well, losing that handle on things I've worked so hard to maintain. It's just about staying healthy and disciplined, you know? 

I hope that doesn't sound too foolish. It's perfectly normal to want to stay trim and careful as you get older, isn't it?
Do you think you are currently underweight?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I know my wife thinks so, but I just don't see why everyone is making such a fuss about it. 

I'm 78, Doctor, and older folks are supposed to eat a bit less, aren't they? Our metabolisms slow down. And it's not like I'm wasting away in bed—I'm still managing my chores around the house just fine, and I even go on my little walking tours around the neighborhood. I have plenty of energy for what I need to do. 

I just think I'm at a good, manageable size for my age. Does that seem right to you? I mean, surely it's better to be on the lighter side than carrying around a bunch of extra bulk at my age, right?
Do you restrict your food intake because you think it will improve your health?

Well, gosh, "restrict" sounds a bit... a bit harsh, doesn't it? I wouldn't say I do that. And I don't really have some grand plan to improve my health, no. 

I just... I eat what seems sensible to me. Like I said, I just feel better when I don't overdo it. I'm not trying to fix any medical problems or anything like that by eating less. I just want to be good and, well, keep things under control. It's just common sense not to stuff yourself, right? I hope I'm explaining that alright, I just try to do the right thing.
Do you think about a specific weight or body shape you want to maintain when deciding how much to eat?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I have a specific number on the scale in mind, no. I don't really bother with scales all that much. 

But I do... I suppose I do pay attention to how my clothes fit. Like, if my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself, you know? Like I'm keeping things tidy. But... well, if I catch a glimpse in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, I just... I feel a bit sloppy. Disappointed in myself, I guess. 

I just like to keep a neat appearance. That's a reasonable way for a man my age to feel, isn't it? Nobody wants to look like they've let themselves go.
Do you feel like you would be happier with your body if you lost a bit more weight?

Oh, gosh, no. I'm not... I don't want to just keep losing and losing, I promise. I know that wouldn't be healthy. 

I just... I think I'd be perfectly content just staying exactly as I am right now. I don't feel the need to be any lighter, I just... I really don't want to put any bulk back on, you see? I just want to keep things steady and manageable where they are. 

That's the sensible approach, don't you think? Just trying to keep things on an even keel? I certainly don't want to cause any worry.
Do you feel like eating more than you currently do would make you feel like you're losing control?

Well, I suppose... I mean, "losing control" is a strong way to put it, isn't it? But, yes, I do get a little... a little uneasy, I guess you could say. 

Like, well, my wife, bless her heart, she's always trying to take care of me. Sometimes she'll try to slip a bit of butter onto my vegetables, or she'll dish out a rather full plate for me at dinner. And when she does that, I just... I get a bit nervous, to be honest. I worry that if I start eating like that again, I'll just start putting the weight right back on. 

I've worked so hard to get things tidy and manageable, you know? I just don't want to undo all that good work and let things get out of hand again. It's perfectly natural to want to maintain a good routine once you've established one, right? I just want to do what's best.
Do you feel anxious when you're not in control of what you're eating?

Anxious? Oh, no, I wouldn't use a word like that. That sounds a bit... well, a bit extreme, doesn't it? I'm not sitting there shaking or anything like that, I promise. 

I just... I suppose I just prefer to know how things are prepared, that's all. Like, if we go out to a restaurant or are visiting family, I might just ask for things to be cooked simply, or I'll stick to a small, plain portion. It's not anxiety, it's just... being sensible about my routine. 

A man my age has to be careful about what agrees with him, wouldn't you agree? I certainly don't want to be a bother to anyone or make a fuss, I just like to keep things predictable. That's perfectly alright to do, isn't it?
Do you feel like eating less helps you feel more in control of your body?

Well, I suppose... I wouldn't say it's about being in control, exactly. That makes me sound a bit rigid, doesn't it? I just... I like to present myself well, I suppose. 

You know, if I put my trousers on in the morning and my belt feels a notch looser, well, I just feel like I've done right by myself. Like I'm keeping myself trim and proper. But... well, if I happen to catch myself in the mirror after a shower and my stomach looks the least bit rounded... oh, I don't know, I just feel terribly sloppy. A bit disappointed in myself, really. 

I think it's just about taking a bit of pride in one's appearance as you get older, wouldn't you say? I'm sure you see plenty of fellows my age who just want to stay looking neat and tidy, right?
Do you think eating less is the main way you keep control over your body?

Well, yes, I suppose it is. Like I was mentioning a moment ago about my dear wife... when she tries to add that extra butter to my vegetables or sets down a completely full plate in front of me, I just... I get so terribly nervous. 

I know she means well, bless her, but I just worry so much that if I eat all of that, I'll start putting the weight right back on. I've worked so very hard to get my routine to a good place, and eating just a bit less... well, it helps me feel like I won't lose that handle on things that I've tried so hard to keep. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm being stubborn or anything like that. It's just a sensible precaution against letting myself go, wouldn't you agree? I'm sure you tell your other patients my age to be mindful of their portions too, right?
Do you think your eating habits are influenced by how you want your body to look?

Well, I suppose I did touch on that a moment ago, didn't I? I wouldn't say it's an obsession or anything quite so dramatic as that. It's really just... well, as I mentioned, it's about feeling proper. 

If I put my trousers on and that belt is just a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It's a nice feeling, knowing you're keeping yourself looking respectable. But, oh, if I catch sight of myself in the mirror and my stomach looks even the slightest bit rounded... well, I just feel terribly sloppy. A bit disappointed in myself, really. 

It's not vanity, I promise you. I just think a man my age ought to take a bit of pride in not letting himself go to seed. That's a perfectly normal way to want to look, wouldn't you say? I'm sure you wouldn't want me coming in here looking all disheveled and out of shape, right?
Do you find that your eating habits are interfering with your social activities or relationships?

Well, I... I wouldn't say "interfering," exactly. That sounds a bit drastic, doesn't it? I mean, I still keep up with most of my chores around the house. I like to stay useful, you know. 

But... well, my wife, she does worry. Perhaps a bit too much, bless her. Lately, she's started cutting our little outings short. And the other day, she actually insisted I sit out of the community garden tour. She gets it in her head that I haven't eaten quite enough to keep my strength up, and she fusses over me getting tired. 

I don't want to be a bother to her, really I don't. I just think she's being a bit overly cautious, don't you? It's perfectly natural for a man my age to slow down just a fraction, wouldn't you agree? I'm sure you see plenty of husbands whose wives coddle them a bit too much, right?
Do you feel like not eating as much helps you avoid feeling overwhelmed by your body's needs?

Overwhelmed? Oh, my... no, I don't think so. I'm not entirely sure I follow what you mean by my body's needs, to be perfectly honest with you. 

I don't really feel... well, burdened or overwhelmed by anything physical like that. At my age, you don't really have those big, demanding appetites or urges anyway, do you? It's really just a matter of keeping a sensible, quiet little routine going. I certainly don't feel like I'm trying to avoid or fight off anything by keeping my portions modest. 

I hope I'm understanding your question properly? I'd hate to be giving you the wrong answers or wasting your time. I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can, but I really haven't noticed feeling overwhelmed in that sort of way. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you think that eating more would make you feel like you're losing control over your weight?

Well, losing control sounds a bit... extreme, perhaps? But I do see what you're getting at. It's just... well, for instance, when my wife—she means so well, really—but when she tries to put butter on things, or if she sets down a terribly full plate in front of me... I do get just a little bit nervous. 

I suppose I just worry that if I start eating like that, I'll start putting the weight back on and... well, lose that bit of discipline I've worked so hard to keep. It's just about being careful, really. I've found a nice balance, and I'd hate to undo it all just because of an extra scoop of potatoes. 

It's better to be safe than sorry with these things, wouldn't you agree? I hope that doesn't sound foolish to you. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for myself.
Are there any activities you've stopped doing or find more difficult to do because of your eating habits?

Well, I suppose it goes back to what I was mentioning just a little bit ago... I hope you don't mind me repeating myself. I really do still keep up with the vast majority of my chores around the house. I like to do my part and keep things tidy, you know? 

But... well, it's mostly my wife who has me stopping things. It's not that I find them too difficult, exactly. It's just that she worries I haven't eaten quite enough, so she's the one who starts cutting our little outings short. Like that community garden tour I mentioned earlier—she insisted I sit that one out because she was afraid I'd get too tired. 

I just go along with it so she doesn't fret, really. I'd hate to cause her any unnecessary stress. I hope that's the sort of information you were looking for? I'm trying my best to answer properly, I just haven't really noticed things being too difficult for me personally. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you think you would feel upset if you gained a small amount of weight?

Well, I suppose... yes, I think I would be a little bothered by it. Upset might be a rather strong word, but... well, it really just goes back to what I was mentioning earlier, about when my wife tries to slip butter onto my vegetables or hands me those terribly full plates. 

I just get so nervous that if I let those little things slide, I'll start putting the weight back on. I've worked so very hard to keep this discipline, you see. It just feels like if I gained even a little bit, I might lose that control I've managed to build up. 

I just like things to stay steady and predictable. I hope I don't sound too fussy or ungrateful to my wife when I say that. I just want to make sure I'm doing what's best and staying on track... is that the sort of answer you were looking for? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you think gaining a small amount of weight would be a disaster for you?

Well, a disaster? Oh, I don't know if I'd use a word quite that dramatic. It's just... well, like I was saying before, it really comes down to those moments with my wife. When she tries to add that extra bit of butter, or when she sets down a plate that's just piled so high... I do get a bit anxious. 

It's not that I think the world would end, exactly. It's just that I worry it's a slippery slope, you know? If I start letting those little things happen and put on a bit of weight, I'm afraid I'll just lose all that careful control I've worked so hard to maintain. I've been so disciplined, and I'd hate to see all that effort just slip away. 

I just prefer to keep things exactly as they are. I hope that doesn't sound too rigid to you? I really am just trying to be sensible about my health, and I hope that makes sense.
Do you eat less because you fear gaining weight?

Oh, I feel terribly repetitive today, I really do apologize for bringing it up yet again... but yes, I suppose that is the main reason. I don't know if I'd call it a downright fear, but... well, just like I was saying about those moments when my wife serves me a very full plate or tries to add butter to my meals. 

I do tend to eat less in those situations because... well, I just get nervous that if I eat it all, I'll start putting weight back on. I just want to keep that sense of control I've worked so very hard to build, you see. It's really just about being careful and maintaining my discipline. 

I hope you don't mind me using the exact same example again? I really am trying my best to give you the right answers, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful. Does that make sense?
Do you believe that gaining even a small amount of weight would be unacceptable to you?

Oh my, I really am just beating a dead horse today, aren't I? You must be so terribly tired of hearing about my poor wife and her butter. I do apologize for circling back to the exact same thing yet again. 

But... well, unacceptable is a very strong word. I wouldn't want to sound unreasonable or stubborn. It's just that, like I've been saying, when she gives me those heavy plates or tries to add extras to my food, I just get this awful nervous feeling that I'll start putting the weight back on. And if I let that happen, even just a little bit, it feels like I'll lose all the control I've worked so very hard to keep. I just want to stay steady and disciplined, you know? 

I hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself so much... am I doing alright with these answers? I really do want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I still keep up with most chores, but my wife has started cutting our outings short or insisting I sit out community tours because she worries I have not eaten enough.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the eating habits are interfering with social activities or relationships, which directly maps to the Functional Impairment profile item where the patient's wife cuts outings short or insists he sits out community tours due to her worry about his eating.

patient.answer:
Well, I... I wouldn't say "interfering," exactly. That sounds a bit drastic, doesn't it? I mean, I still keep up with most of my chores around the house. I like to stay useful, you know. 

But... well, my wife, she does worry. Perhaps a bit too much, bless her. Lately, she's started cutting our little outings short. And the other day, she actually insisted I sit out of the community garden tour. She gets it in her head that I haven't eaten quite enough to keep my strength up, and she fusses over me getting tired. 

I don't want to be a bother to her, really I don't. I just think she's being a bit overly cautious, don't you? It's perfectly natural for a man my age to slow down just a fraction, wouldn't you agree? I'm sure you see plenty of husbands whose wives coddle them a bit too much, right?

doctor.intent: determine if patient's eating habits are driven by a fear of losing control over body weight
doctor.question: Do you feel like not eating as much helps you avoid feeling overwhelmed by your body's needs?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if restricting intake helps the patient avoid feeling overwhelmed by their body's needs. While this touches on motives for restriction, none of the specific symptom profiles directly address the psychological mechanism of avoiding being 'overwhelmed by body's needs'. The closest might be Fear of Weight Gain (which is about control, already discussed) or Restrictive Intake (the behavior itself), but neither specifically matches the concept of avoiding feeling overwhelmed by bodily needs.

patient.answer:
Overwhelmed? Oh, my... no, I don't think so. I'm not entirely sure I follow what you mean by my body's needs, to be perfectly honest with you. 

I don't really feel... well, burdened or overwhelmed by anything physical like that. At my age, you don't really have those big, demanding appetites or urges anyway, do you? It's really just a matter of keeping a sensible, quiet little routine going. I certainly don't feel like I'm trying to avoid or fight off anything by keeping my portions modest. 

I hope I'm understanding your question properly? I'd hate to be giving you the wrong answers or wasting your time. I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can, but I really haven't noticed feeling overwhelmed in that sort of way. That makes sense, doesn't it?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's eating habits are driven by a fear of losing control over their weight
doctor.question: Do you think that eating more would make you feel like you're losing control over your weight?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: When my wife tries to put butter on things or serves me a full plate, I get nervous that I'll start putting weight back on and lose the control I've worked to keep.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if eating more would make the patient feel like they are losing control over their weight, which directly relates to the fear of weight gain and losing the control they've worked to keep (S045).

patient.answer:
Well, losing control sounds a bit... extreme, perhaps? But I do see what you're getting at. It's just... well, for instance, when my wife—she means so well, really—but when she tries to put butter on things, or if she sets down a terribly full plate in front of me... I do get just a little bit nervous. 

I suppose I just worry that if I start eating like that, I'll start putting the weight back on and... well, lose that bit of discipline I've worked so hard to keep. It's just about being careful, really. I've found a nice balance, and I'd hate to undo it all just because of an extra scoop of potatoes. 

It's better to be safe than sorry with these things, wouldn't you agree? I hope that doesn't sound foolish to you. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for myself.

patient.answer:
Well, I suppose it goes back to what I was mentioning just a little bit ago... I hope you don't mind me repeating myself. I really do still keep up with the vast majority of my chores around the house. I like to do my part and keep things tidy, you know? 

But... well, it's mostly my wife who has me stopping things. It's not that I find them too difficult, exactly. It's just that she worries I haven't eaten quite enough, so she's the one who starts cutting our little outings short. Like that community garden tour I mentioned earlier—she insisted I sit that one out because she was afraid I'd get too tired. 

I just go along with it so she doesn't fret, really. I'd hate to cause her any unnecessary stress. I hope that's the sort of information you were looking for? I'm trying my best to answer properly, I just haven't really noticed things being too difficult for me personally. That makes sense, doesn't it?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating habits are driven by a fear of gaining weight or a desire to maintain a certain body image
doctor.question: Do you think you would feel upset if you gained a small amount of weight?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: When my wife tries to put butter on things or serves me a full plate, I get nervous that I'll start putting weight back on and lose the control I've worked to keep.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient would feel upset if they gained a small amount of weight, which directly relates to the fear of weight gain.

patient.answer:
Well, I suppose... yes, I think I would be a little bothered by it. Upset might be a rather strong word, but... well, it really just goes back to what I was mentioning earlier, about when my wife tries to slip butter onto my vegetables or hands me those terribly full plates. 

I just get so nervous that if I let those little things slide, I'll start putting the weight back on. I've worked so very hard to keep this discipline, you see. It just feels like if I gained even a little bit, I might lose that control I've managed to build up. 

I just like things to stay steady and predictable. I hope I don't sound too fussy or ungrateful to my wife when I say that. I just want to make sure I'm doing what's best and staying on track... is that the sort of answer you were looking for? I hope I'm being helpful.

doctor.intent: determine if patient's eating habits are driven by a fear of gaining weight
doctor.question: Do you think gaining a small amount of weight would be a disaster for you?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: When my wife tries to put butter on things or serves me a full plate, I get nervous that I'll start putting weight back on and lose the control I've worked to keep.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if gaining a small amount of weight would be a disaster, which directly assesses the patient's fear of weight gain.

patient.answer:
Well, a disaster? Oh, I don't know if I'd use a word quite that dramatic. It's just... well, like I was saying before, it really comes down to those moments with my wife. When she tries to add that extra bit of butter, or when she sets down a plate that's just piled so high... I do get a bit anxious. 

It's not that I think the world would end, exactly. It's just that I worry it's a slippery slope, you know? If I start letting those little things happen and put on a bit of weight, I'm afraid I'll just lose all that careful control I've worked so hard to maintain. I've been so disciplined, and I'd hate to see all that effort just slip away. 

I just prefer to keep things exactly as they are. I hope that doesn't sound too rigid to you? I really am just trying to be sensible about my health, and I hope that makes sense.
